The initial cost to plant the tree is $90.  
Each year, the tree produces 7 lemons, sold for $1.50 each, giving an annual revenue of 7 × $1.50 = $10.50.  
The annual cost to water and feed the tree is $3, so the net profit per year is $10.50 – $3 = $7.50.  

To recover the $90 initial investment and start earning money (total profit > $0), the number of years \( t \) must satisfy:  
$7.50 × t > $90  
t > 90 / 7.50  
t > 12  

Since t must be a whole number of years, it takes 13 years for total earnings to exceed total costs.  
After 12 years, total profit is exactly $90 (break-even), so he starts earning money in the 13th year.

Answer: 13
